_: MORROWIND's rules, written out flat and NEVER tuned. This file is the fixed half of the known-answer test: TES III's pacing is documented (level 2 in the first hour or two, the main quest finishing around level 20-25 at ~40 h, 45-55 by 150 h, a use-levelling ceiling of 78), so if our engine cannot reproduce it from Morrowind's own numbers the engine is wrong. When the test fails, tune data/content-vvardenfell.json - the estimate - not this. Sources: UESP Morrowind:Skills and the individual skill pages; Morrowind:Leveling; Morrowind:Attributes (health per level).
label: TES III: Morrowind (Vvardenfell)

rankCost._: pointsToNextRank = (skill+1) * classFactor * specFactor - identical to ours, which is the point.

levelTrigger._: Ten major/minor ranks bank a level, taken at a rest. Misc ranks NEVER count - which is exactly why Morrowind's practical ceiling is 78 rather than the ~124 our 3:1 tail would allow, and why an all-misc character can play for a hundred hours and stay level 1.

vastei._: Morrowind has no vastei; it hands out three attribute points at a sitting, multiplied by the skill-use multiplier table. We keep our own currency here purely so the engine has something to spend - the known-answer test reads levels and skills, never attributes.

attributePurchase._: Ours, borrowed. Not part of the answer being checked.

health._: Starting health = (Strength + Endurance)/2. Each level adds 0.1 * your endurance AT THAT MOMENT and the grant is NOT retroactive, which is the whole reason Morrowind players front-load Endurance. Modelled as a running total rather than a formula.

use._: Morrowind's flat, magnitude-blind use values. A rat and a golden saint are worth the same point.
